messages:
aj_sales: Quick sync — Prospect 'Gauntlet' wants to run a 2-week POC to validate migration from CompetitorX. Main asks: prompt parity, response diffs, SLA/egress IPs, pricing for burst + reserved, and security questionnaire answers. Can we run this timeline? Who owns KMS + customer data flow doc?

maria-devrel: I can lead the POC plan. Proposed split: week1 functional parity (endpoints + prompts), week2 scale/latency + pricing validation. Need a small sample app from them (10 endpoints).

aj_sales: They can provide a Postman collection and example prompt set. Also ask for any system messages they use.

maria-devrel: Perfect — I'll map their API surface. Quick note on differences we typically see: CompetitorX uses `model_id` and `max_tokens` in request body, while we use `model` and `max_output_tokens`. Also they return a single `response.choices[0].text` blob vs our streaming chunks. I'll prepare a compatibility shim example.

ben_infra: For POC infra: if they want predictable latency we should offer a small Dedicated pool (2 GPUs) with static egress IPs and VPC peering. Lead time ~48h to provision + firewall rules. If they stay on hosted, explain burst throttling behavior.

karim-sec: Security checklist highlights they always ask about: SOC2 status, data residency, encryption in transit & at rest, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs retention, and whether we persist prompts/logs by default. We should also ask customer for their DPA + any encryption key ownership needs.

maria-devrel: Sample shim for their call -> our API (quick example):
```bash
# CompetitorX style
curl https://api.competitorx.com/v1/generate -X POST -d '{"model_id":"x-large","prompt":"Summarize...","max_tokens":150}' 

# Redwood equivalent (we prefer explicit streaming flag)
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -X POST -d '{"model":"x-large","prompt":"Summarize...","max_output_tokens":150,"stream":false}'
```
I'll add a tiny adapter snippet to normalize their `response.choices[0].text` to our `output` shape.

aj_sales: Pricing question from buyer: they want a comparison for 100k tokens/day with occasional spikes to 1M tokens/day. Can someone draft an estimate (hosted vs dedicated commit)? Include quantization/throughput tradeoffs.

ben_infra: Draft numbers: hosted (pay-as-you-go): ~ $0.25 per 1k tokens (example) -> est $25/day base, spikes add $225; Dedicated 1/yr commit (small pool) amortized looks cheaper for sustained usage. I'll put a spreadsheet. Also callout: caching/prefix KV will reduce token burn if prompts are templated.

karim-sec: For the security questionnaire — I'll prepare a short answers doc with links to SOC2 report, KMS integration flow, and sample logging config (what's masked by default). Also flag: if they require HSM + customer-managed keys we need Eng + Legal signoff; takes ~2–3 weeks.

deploy-bot: staging cluster provisioned: gauntlet-poc-202 in us-west1. IPs: 34.82.190.10, 34.82.190.11.

maria-devrel: Action items: (1) @ben_infra to share prov cost spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow; (2) @karim-sec to draft security answers and HSM checklist; (3) @maria-devrel will produce the compatibility shim + sample adapter and a runbook for prompts. Target: kickoff with Gauntlet on Monday.

aj_sales: Noted — I’ll sync with their engineering lead and secure the Postman collection. Please add any blockers here. :thumbsup:
